# Network Checklist: AWS Network Foundation

**Purpose**: Review requirements quality for security, resilience, operability, cost, Terraform state safety, and acceptance-criteria completeness
**Created**: 2026-10-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Security and Exposure Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Are identity, account, and cross-account access boundaries for network provisioning specified with least-privilege requirements? [Completeness, Constitution §I, Plan §State and Provider Configuration]
- [ ] CHK002 Are allowed public ingress sources, protocols, ports, and approval authority defined clearly enough to distinguish approved load-balancer exposure from all other public ingress? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-017, Plan §Validation, Security, and Plan Gates]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the specification define whether NAT-based outbound access is unrestricted or destination-filtered, including any required protocol or destination constraints? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Are endpoint service scope, endpoint policies, subnet or route-table scope, and the relationship to IAM permissions defined for each workload-declared endpoint? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009, Plan §VPC Endpoint Policy]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements for handling security-scan findings and justified exceptions clear, including who approves a suppression and how its rationale is recorded? [Completeness, Constitution §VII, Plan §Validation, Security, and Plan Gates]

## Resilience and Cost Requirements

- [ ] CHK006 Are the shared NAT gateway's AZ failure impact, cross-AZ routing implications, and expected egress behavior documented as acceptance criteria for the chosen default? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK007 Are network availability or recovery targets defined, or is the absence of service-level targets explicitly assigned to workload specifications? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria, Constitution §VI]
- [ ] CHK008 Are cost limits or required cost-approval thresholds defined for shared versus per-AZ NAT, or is cost review explicitly qualitative? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Validation, Security, and Plan Gates]
- [ ] CHK009 Are endpoint unavailability and NAT failure scenarios covered with clear expected routing, degraded-service, and recovery requirements? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009]

## Operability and Terraform State Safety

- [ ] CHK010 Are network observability requirements defined for traffic flow records, route/NAT health signals, retention, and operational ownership, or explicitly excluded from this feature? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, Plan §Module and Environment Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK011 Are remote-state encryption, versioning, locking, backend ownership, and recovery requirements sufficiently explicit to review before an environment plan? [Completeness, Constitution §III, Spec §FR-016, Plan §State and Provider Configuration]
- [ ] CHK012 Are environment-specific state keys and read/write permissions defined so production state cannot be accessed through non-production authorization? [Security, Spec §FR-016, Plan §State and Provider Configuration]
- [ ] CHK013 Are lock contention, stale-lock recovery, and state restoration requirements defined without encouraging unsafe force-unlock or stale-state replacement? [Gap, Constitution §III, Plan §Migration and Rollback]
- [ ] CHK014 Are ownership discovery, import approval, rollback triggers, and recovery steps clear for both newly created and potentially pre-existing network resources? [Completeness, Constitution §II, Plan §Migration and Rollback]

## Acceptance Criteria Completeness

- [ ] CHK015 Can each functional requirement be traced to an objective acceptance scenario or success criterion, including required module outputs for ECS, EKS, RDS, and load balancers? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001–FR-017, Spec §Success Criteria, Plan §Typed Input and Output Contract]
- [ ] CHK016 Are DNS enablement, IPv4-only scope, and the prohibition on direct workload public IPs each covered by measurable acceptance criteria? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK017 Are CIDR allocation ownership, containment, overlap, capacity, and validation failure outcomes specified precisely enough for acceptance review? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Spec §Edge Cases, Plan §Module and Environment Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK018 Are missing or unavailable endpoint services and invalid endpoint policies covered by explicit acceptance outcomes, not only listed as edge cases? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Are permitted application-to-data flows objectively distinguishable by source, destination, protocol, port range, and rationale in both the requirements and acceptance criteria? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK020 Are acceptance criteria for required tags, naming, provider/account guard, and state separation explicit and measurable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-016, Plan §Naming and Tags, Plan §State and Provider Configuration]

## Requirement Consistency and Scope

- [ ] CHK021 Is the boundary between the reusable network module and sandbox environment composition consistent across the specification, plan, and module contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Plan §Module and Environment Boundaries, Plan §Project Structure]
- [ ] CHK022 Are the initial sandbox delivery scope and the later development, staging, and production requirements clearly distinguished so reviewers know what this feature must deliver? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016, Plan §Module and Environment Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK023 Are the no-fixed-endpoint-baseline decision and workload-specific endpoint policy requirements consistent across the spec, plan, and contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §VPC Endpoint Policy]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when requirements still need clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference; this checklist is separate from the built-in specification quality checklist.
